name: Test Company

verdict.title: Strong buy candidate
verdict.summary: High-quality business, healthy balance sheet, no warning signs, and the price is below its estimated fair value. It passes every check in this tool. Before buying, read the business check below and run the deep-dive research.

sellIf: It stops passing the Shariah screen.
Its quality score falls below 50 (now 88): returns on capital are collapsing.
Revenue shrinks two years in a row without a clear, temporary reason.
Debt climbs above 3 times yearly cash earnings (EBITDA); it is 0.5× now.
The reason you bought it no longer holds. Re-check the five questions after every quarterly report.

points: Earned 15%+ on invested capital in 6 of the last 6 years. Without protection from competitors, returns that high usually get competed away.
Margins stayed steady (moved only 0.0 points in 5 years), a sign of pricing power.
Revenue grew in 5 of the last 5 years.

questions.q: Why will this company be bigger in 5 to 10 years?
questions.hint: Track record: revenue grew about 10% a year, and 10% recently. Ask whether the reasons behind that growth are still in place.

questions.q: What protects it from competitors (its moat)?
questions.hint: Strong evidence in the numbers. Something is protecting its profits: find out what (brand, network effects, switching costs, scale).

questions.q: What could break the business (new technology like AI, new rivals, regulation)?
questions.hint: No warning signs in the recent numbers yet. Disruption often shows up in the news before it shows up in the numbers.

questions.q: Is management trustworthy and sensible with your money?
Why is the price where it is?
questions.hint: The price assumes about 2% growth a year vs. 10% in the past. Decide who you believe: the market or the track record.

claudePrompt:
Act as a patient investing mentor for a beginner long-term investor (several-year holds, strictly halal stocks only).
A fundamentals screener analyzed Test Co (TST) at $50.00. Verdict: Strong buy candidate.
Scores: quality 88/100, balance sheet 88/100, revenue growth 10%/yr, valuation Undervalued (fair value ~$79.84, range $50.59-$110; price implies 2% growth/yr vs 10% historically). Shariah screen: passes the AAOIFI-style ratios.
Use web search and cite sources. Explain simply:
1) How it makes money. 2) Its moat, and whether it is getting stronger or weaker. 3) The biggest threats over the next 5 years (AI or tech disruption, competitors, regulation), with recent news. 4) Management quality: track record, insider buying/selling, use of cash. 5) Who is right about future growth, the market or the track record? 6) Halal status on Zoya or Musaffa.
Finish with a clear call (buy now, buy gradually, wait for a lower price, or avoid), the 3 main reasons, and what would change your mind.
strengths: Earns about 18% a year on the money invested in the business (15%+ is excellent).
Profits are fully backed by real cash flow.
Price is below the estimated fair value of about $80.

shariah.headline: Passes the AAOIFI-style screen

standard.name: AAOIFI Shariah Standard No. 21 (financial paper), ratio thresholds
rules: Business: the company's main activity (SEC industry code, plus a name and ticker check for gambling, alcohol and pork) must not be prohibited. Unknown or mixed industries give REVIEW.

Debt: interest-bearing debt (short- and long-term borrowings, current portion of long-term debt, finance leases tagged with debt; operating leases excluded) divided by current market value must be below 30%.
Cash and securities: cash, cash equivalents and marketable or held-to-maturity securities (all treated as interest-bearing, which is conservative) divided by current market value must be below 30%.

Impermissible income: interest income divided by revenue must be below 5%. When interest income is not reported on its own line, an upper bound is used (a broader income line, or all cash and investments at 6% a year); a bound at or above 5% gives REVIEW, not PASS.
Missing data (no market value, no cash or debt figure, no industry code) gives REVIEW (insufficient data), never PASS.
standard.limits: Uses the latest 10-K/10-Q balance sheet and the latest price (AAOIFI uses market value; some index providers use a 24 or 36-month average, which can give different results near a limit). It cannot see impermissible revenue inside business segments.

shariah.note: Approximation of the AAOIFI method using SEC data and the live price. It cannot see the "less than 5% impermissible revenue" detail inside segments, so always confirm on Zoya or Musaffa before buying.

purification.basis: estimated: cash and investments earning about 4% a year / revenue (interest income is not reported)
purification.note: This company does not report interest income on its own line, so this is an estimate. If Zoya or Musaffa show a purification percentage, use theirs.
